title: Hosea Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hosea chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hosea Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hosea Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Hosea 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The inhabitants of Samaria shall fear
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Israel is an empty vine' appears first in the chapter, as it is the opening line of Hosea 10:1.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:1, what does Israel bring forth?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'he bringeth forth fruit unto himself' which clearly indicates what Israel produces.

questions.question: What will happen to the altars according to Hosea 10:2?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:2 states 'he shall break down their altars', indicating what will happen to them.

questions.question: What does Hosea 10:3 say the people will say?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states 'For now they shall say, We have no king', reflecting the sentiments of the people.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:4, what have they spoken?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:4 mentions 'They have spoken words, swearing falsely', indicating the nature of their speech.

questions.question: What will spring up as judgment according to Hosea 10:4?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:4 states 'thus judgment springeth up as hemlock in the furrows of the field', referring to the nature of judgment.

questions.question: Who shall fear because of the calves of Bethaven according to Hosea 10:5?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:5 clearly states 'The inhabitants of Samaria shall fear because of the calves of Bethaven', identifying who will fear.

questions.question: What will the priests of Samaria do according to Hosea 10:5?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions 'the priests thereof shall mourn over it', indicating their reaction to the situation.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:1, what have they made because of the goodness of their land?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'according to the goodness of his land they have made goodly images' indicates what was made.

questions.question: What is said about their heart in Hosea 10:2?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:2 states 'Their heart is divided', describing the state of their hearts.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:3, why do they say they have no king?
options: Because they feared not the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Because they feared not the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse states 'because we feared not the LORD; what then should a king do to us?', indicating the reason.

questions.question: The inhabitants of Samaria mourned over the calves of Bethaven. True or False?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:5 indicates that 'the people thereof shall mourn over it', confirming this statement is true.

questions.question: Israel's heart is described as whole. True or False?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:2 states 'Their heart is divided', indicating that this statement is false.

questions.question: The priests of Samaria rejoiced over the calves of Bethaven. True or False?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:5 indicates that the priests mourned, not rejoiced, making this statement false.

questions.question: The covenant made by the people was true. True or False?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:4 mentions 'swearing falsely in making a covenant', indicating the covenant was not true.

medium.title: Hosea Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hosea Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to Ephraim according to Hosea 10:6?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:6 states that Ephraim shall receive shame and Israel shall be ashamed of his own counsel.

questions.question: What does Hosea 10:2 promise will happen if someone has a divided heart as stated in the verse?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:2 states that their heart is divided and now shall they be found faulty.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:7, what is said about the king of Samaria?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:7 states that her king is cut off as the foam upon the water.

questions.question: What does Hosea 10:4 indicate about the words spoken in making a covenant?
options: They are false and lead to judgment
questions.correctAnswer: They are false and lead to judgment
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:4 mentions that they have spoken words, swearing falsely in making a covenant, leading to judgment.

questions.question: What will happen to the high places of Aven according to Hosea 10:8?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:8 states that the high places of Aven, the sin of Israel, shall be destroyed.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:9, how long has Israel been sinning?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:9 states that Israel has sinned from the days of Gibeah.

questions.question: What does Hosea 10:10 indicate about God's desire regarding the people?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:10 states that it is in God's desire that He should chastise them.

questions.question: What does Hosea 10:5 say about the inhabitants of Samaria?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:5 states that the inhabitants of Samaria shall fear because of the calves of Bethaven.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:3, why will the people say they have no king?
options: Because they feared not the LORD
Because they wanted a new king
Because they have a strong leader
questions.correctAnswer: Because they feared not the LORD
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:3 states they shall say, 'We have no king, because we feared not the LORD.'

questions.question: What is the result of Israel's multiplied fruit as stated in Hosea 10:1?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:1 states that according to the multitude of his fruit he hath increased the altars.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:2, what will happen to their altars?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:2 states that he shall break down their altars.

questions.question: The statement 'O Israel, thou hast sinned from the days of Gibeah' is found in which verse?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:9 specifically states that Israel has sinned from the days of Gibeah.

questions.question: Is it true that the high places of Aven will be left untouched according to Hosea 10:8?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:8 states that the high places of Aven shall be destroyed.

questions.question: Is it true that the king of Samaria is compared to foam upon the water according to Hosea 10:7?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:7 states that her king is cut off as the foam upon the water.

questions.question: Is it true that God expresses a desire to bless Israel in Hosea 10:10?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hosea 10:10 indicates that it is in God's desire to chastise them, not to bless them.

hard.title: Hosea Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hosea Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Hosea 10:11, Ephraim is compared to what kind of animal that is taught and loves to tread out the corn?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:11 explicitly states, 'And Ephraim is as an heifer that is taught, and loveth to tread out the corn;' making 'Heifer' the correct answer.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:12, what are the Israelites instructed to sow and reap?
options: Sow in righteousness, reap in mercy
Sow in mercy, reap in righteousness
Sow in faith, reap in hope
Sow in fear, reap in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Sow in righteousness, reap in mercy
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:12 commands, 'Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap in mercy;' making this the correct response.

questions.question: What consequence does Hosea 10:13 say results from trusting in their own ways and mighty men?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:13 states, 'Ye have eaten the fruit of lies: because thou didst trust in thy way, in the multitude of thy mighty men.'

questions.question: Hosea 10:14 references a violent event involving Shalman spoiling Betharbel. What tragic act is mentioned?
options: The mother was dashed in pieces upon her children
The city was burned to the ground
questions.correctAnswer: The mother was dashed in pieces upon her children
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:14 describes, '...as Shalman spoiled Betharbel in the day of battle: the mother was dashed in pieces upon her children.'

questions.question: What does Hosea 10:15 predict will happen to the king of Israel because of great wickedness?
options: He shall be utterly cut off in a morning
He shall be exalted by God
He shall be taken captive to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be utterly cut off in a morning
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:15 states, 'in a morning shall the king of Israel utterly be cut off' because of great wickedness.

questions.question: According to Hosea 10:11, which tribe is said to plow and break clods respectively?
options: Judah shall plow, and Jacob shall break his clods
Ephraim shall plow, and Judah shall break clods
Jacob shall plow, and Ephraim shall break clods
Judah shall plow, and Ephraim shall break clods
questions.correctAnswer: Judah shall plow, and Jacob shall break his clods
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:11 says, 'Judah shall plow, and Jacob shall break his clods,' specifying these roles for the tribes.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'zara' (זָרַע) in Hosea 10:12 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'zara' (זָרַע) used in Hosea 10:12 means 'to sow,' as in 'Sow to yourselves in righteousness'.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Hosea 10:12 in the phrase 'Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap in mercy'?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:12 uses parallelism by balancing 'sow in righteousness' with 'reap in mercy', a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of sowing righteousness and reaping mercy found in Hosea 10:12?
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:7-8 reflects the principle of sowing and reaping righteousness and iniquity, echoing Hosea 10:12's theme.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event is alluded to in Hosea 10:9 referencing the days of Gibeah?
options: The battle involving the tribe of Benjamin in Judges 19-20
questions.correctAnswer: The battle involving the tribe of Benjamin in Judges 19-20
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:9's mention of Gibeah alludes to the infamous civil war against Benjamin described in Judges 19-20.

questions.question: What precedes Hosea 10:12 in the context of Israel's spiritual state?
options: Ephraim is likened to a taught heifer loving to tread the corn
The inhabitants of Samaria fear because of the calves of Bethaven
Israel is called an empty vine
Their heart is divided and they are found faulty
questions.correctAnswer: Ephraim is likened to a taught heifer loving to tread the corn
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:11 directly precedes verse 12 and compares Ephraim to a taught heifer that loves to tread out corn.

questions.question: What literary device is employed in Hosea 10:14's description of Shalman's destruction of Betharbel?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:14 uses graphic imagery in describing the mother dashed upon her children to communicate the horror of the defeat.

questions.question: Which verse in Hosea 10 expresses the theme of broken altars and images due to Israel’s fruitfulness?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:1 states 'Israel is an empty vine... according to the multitude of his fruit he hath increased the altars...' linking fruitfulness to idolatry.

questions.question: Does Hosea 10:3 suggest that Israel's lack of fear of the LORD results in having no king?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:3 says, 'For now they shall say, We have no king, because we feared not the LORD,' confirming the connection.

questions.question: Is it true that Hosea 10:8 describes the high places of Aven as flourishing and prosperous?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:8 states the high places of Aven shall be destroyed, overgrown with thorns and thistles, opposite of flourishing.

theological.title: Hosea Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hosea Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hosea 10:1 teach about human sin?
options: Human sin leads to self-centered fruitfulness that fosters idolatry
Human sin is primarily ignorance of the law
Human sin can be overcome by good works alone
Human sin is excusable due to cultural context
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin leads to self-centered fruitfulness that fosters idolatry
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:1 describes Israel as an 'empty vine' that brings forth fruit unto itself and increases altars and images, indicating self-centered sin expressed in idolatry.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenant faithfulness does Hosea 10:4 teach?
options: False swearing in covenant leads to judgment
Covenants can be broken without consequence
God ignores false covenants if intentions are good
Covenants are irrelevant to divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: False swearing in covenant leads to judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 10:4 states that they swore falsely in making a covenant and thus judgment springs up as hemlock, underscoring God's justice against covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine chastisement is taught in Hosea 10:10?
options: God desires to chastise sinners to bring repentance
Chastisement is unnecessary for the elect
questions.correctAnswer: God desires to chastise sinners to bring repentance
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:10 reveals God's desire to chastise and gather the people, implying correction aimed at repentance rather than mere punishment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hosea 10:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:3 mentions Israel saying 'We have no king,' reflecting God's sovereign authority over kingship and judgment upon Israel’s fearlessness toward the LORD.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hosea 10:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 10:12 calls to 'sow in righteousness' and 'reap in mercy,' highlighting God's merciful readiness to pour out righteousness upon repentance.

questions.question: How does Hosea 10:5 connect to the broader biblical theme of idol worship and its consequences?
options: It anticipates the exile as a judgment for idolatry
It shows idolatry as a minor cultural issue
It implies idolatry strengthens Israel's political alliances
It suggests idolatry leads to divine blessing
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the exile as a judgment for idolatry
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:5's mention of Samaria fearing because of the calves of Bethaven foreshadows exile and judgment for idolatry, consistent with Deuteronomy's covenant curses.

questions.question: How does Hosea 10:11 prepare for New Testament themes of sanctification?
options: By depicting divine empowerment for obedient service
By denying human responsibility in sanctification
By emphasizing the futility of human effort
questions.correctAnswer: By depicting divine empowerment for obedient service
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:11 shows God enabling Ephraim to 'ride' and Judah to 'plow,' symbolizing sanctification as God’s enabling work in human obedience, paralleling New Testament sanctification themes.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hosea 10:1 and 10:4 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Human self-centered idolatry leads to covenant unfaithfulness, provoking divine judgment
Human sin is excused if accompanied by ritual sacrifice
God’s judgment is unrelated to human covenant actions
Idolatry is not a significant factor in divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Human self-centered idolatry leads to covenant unfaithfulness, provoking divine judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 10:1 shows idolatry from self-centered fruit, and 10:4 exposes false covenant vows, together teaching that such sin incurs God's just judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hosea 10:10 and 10:12 teach about repentance and divine response?
options: God desires repentance which leads to mercy and righteousness
Repentance is futile before divine wrath
Mercy is granted regardless of repentance
Repentance delays judgment but does not change outcome
questions.correctAnswer: God desires repentance which leads to mercy and righteousness
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:10 describes God's desire to chastise for repentance, and 10:12 calls for seeking the LORD to receive righteousness and mercy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hosea 10:13 and 10:15 teach about the consequences of trusting in human power?
options: Trusting in human might leads to rebellion and ultimate destruction
God blesses those who rely on their armies
Trust in human power is neutral in God’s judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in human might leads to rebellion and ultimate destruction
questions.explanation: Verse 10:13 condemns trusting in mighty men, and 10:15 prophesies destruction of Israel’s king because of wickedness, linking human reliance with downfall.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Hosea 10:14-15 depicts excessive divine cruelty. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God’s judgment is severe but just, responding to great wickedness
God’s wrath is unjust and excessive
The violent imagery is purely symbolic with no real judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is severe but just, responding to great wickedness
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:14-15 describes the spoiling of fortresses and cutting off the king because of great wickedness, emphasizing just divine retribution rather than cruelty.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hosea 10:6 teach about God's interaction with human political powers?
options: God uses foreign powers to execute judgment on Israel
God’s kingdom is separate from earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: God uses foreign powers to execute judgment on Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 10:6 mentions the calves being carried to Assyria as a present, symbolizing God’s use of Assyria to bring shame and judgment on Israel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially evident in Hosea 10:8 concerning judgment on idolatry?
questions.explanation: Hosea 10:8 describes destruction of high places and altars with thorns and thistles, showing God's holiness intolerant of sin and idolatry.

questions.question: How does Hosea 10:9 contribute to the chapter’s theological narrative about Israel's persistent sin?
options: It identifies longstanding sinfulness dating back to Gibeah
It praises Israel’s faithfulness in battle
It suggests Israel’s sin was only recent
It denies Israel’s involvement in iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: It identifies longstanding sinfulness dating back to Gibeah
questions.explanation: Verse 10:9 states Israel has sinned from the days of Gibeah, indicating persistent rebellion and unrepentance throughout history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hosea 10:7 and 10:15 teach about the fate of Israel's leadership?
options: Israel's kingship will be utterly cut off due to sin
Israel’s kingship is secure despite rebellion
Kingship is irrelevant to Israel’s covenant
God will replace Israel’s kings with foreign rulers
questions.correctAnswer: Israel's kingship will be utterly cut off due to sin
questions.explanation: Verse 10:7 mentions the king of Samaria cut off as foam, and 10:15 prophesies the king of Israel being cut off for wickedness, emphasizing judgment on leadership.
